story: US startup Substrate announces chipmaking tool that it says will rival ASML
text: LOL, I recommend highly to everyone who thinks a startup can challenge ASML this 1.38min video: [LINK] Its an industrial flight video through a ASML TWIN Exe HighNAV. Here is also a presentation of ~45min at CCC / Germany (in English language) which I highly recommend to watch: [VIDEO] Especially the explanation how they use two milisecond laser shots to first molt the tin and then distribute it symetrically(!!!) with a second shot across the surface. There IS NO chance that this startup will be able to somehow compete, if even Chinese state actors cant do it (yet).

story: ASML unveils EUV light source advance that could yield 50% more chips by 2030
text: There is an excellent video from German CCC on how chips are produced from their last convention: [VIDEO] I can highly recommend this to everybody who is "somehow in tech or IT"
This was the one that did it for me: "38C3 - From Silicon to Sovereignty: How Advanced Chips Are Redefining Global Dominance" [VIDEO] Absolutely insane stuff.

story: BYD Sells 4.6M Vehicles in 2025, Meets Revised Sales Goal
text: With current military technology it is not really possible, isn't it? [VIDEO] describes it really well. So the question is more about what part of means of defense you outsource. And what parts of means of defense are outsourced by your enemies. You don't want to base your defense on inferior shipbuilding capabilities, do you?
